name: aish
description: An AI-native Linux shell that routes commands and intent to Claude or local LLMs
summary: AI-native shell: type commands to run directly, intent to an agent that plans, executes, and iterates until done.

entrypoints.name: aish-repl
entrypoints.purpose: Interactive REPL shell; entry point for session startup, command routing, and model interaction

entrypoints.name: coordinator-worker
entrypoints.purpose: Persistent background coordinator run; re-executes aish with a task, manages multi-turn agent loops, and returns structured output

entrypoints.name: batch-processor
entrypoints.purpose: Anthropic Batches API integration; queues and monitors async batch runs for cost-optimized bulk agent invocations

modules.purpose: Interactive REPL loop (rustyline); reads user input, routes to dispatch or model, manages `:commands`, attachment UI
Core agentic turn loop; invokes Claude/LLM, processes tool calls, maintains conversation history
LLM provider abstraction; supports Claude API, Grok, and mistral.rs (local inference)
Tool execution layer; implements read_file, write_file, run_program, run_interactive, change_dir, etc.
Direct-dispatch routing; decides whether a line is a real command (run directly) or intent (route to model)
Background worker orchestration; spawns, monitors, resumes durable coordinator runs with persistent context
Per-REPL or per-worker session state; holds cwd, environment, history, backend config, MCP connections
SQLite + sqlite-vec persistence layer; stores input/output history, memories, worker records, and vector embeddings
Model Context Protocol server integration; manages MCP server lifecycle, tool routing, and skill discovery
Docker container lifecycle for background workers; spawns, monitors, cleans up ephemeral worker containers
Git repository utilities; manages branches, commits, pull requests via GitHub API integration
Persistent memory system; stores agent/user facts across sessions via recall/remember tools
Skill discovery and management; loads SKILL.md files from ~/.aish/skills/, advertises to model

patterns.convention: Session is the carrier of per-execution state (cwd, env, history). Mutated in-place by builtins (cd, set, export) and tools; not passed via function return.

patterns.applied_via: Every tool returns anyhow::Result<T>; partial failures (e.g., a read timeout) return Some(output) + Err, preserving partial work.
patterns.convention: Tools never panic; they log, return Err or degraded output, and let the agent decide next steps.
Lines are routed by predicates: `:command` → REPL, word-1 is real binary → direct, else → model. `!` forces direct, `?` forces model.

patterns.applied_via: tools::Decision enum; :mode <paranoid|careful|normal|yolo> sets the gate level per session
patterns.convention: Each tool checks `session.mode` before execution: paranoid=all, careful=writes only, normal=write+delete, yolo=none.

patterns.applied_via: crate::style:: for colors/emphasis; crate::md::render_stdout() for markdown → terminal
patterns.convention: Model responses are markdown; stdout is rendered with colors + emoji. NO_COLOR env disables; piped stdout auto-disables.

patterns.applied_via: timeout_secs (default 120s) on run_program; Ctrl-C caught by tokio::signal::ctrl_c() for turn abort
patterns.convention: Model-run programs are killed after timeout with partial output. Interactive (TTY) programs run to completion and inherit signals.

patterns.applied_via: db.record('input', ...) + db.record('output', ...) after each interactive turn
patterns.convention: All input/output is stored to aish.db for recall; large outputs truncated head-first to 4000 bytes.

patterns.applied_via: sqlite-vec to store embeddings; memory recall uses vector similarity search
patterns.convention: recall tool returns top-K memories by cosine similarity; embeddings are computed lazily on recall.

features.name: command-routing
features.description: Lines are routed: `:commands` → REPL, real binaries → direct dispatch, anything else → model. Escape hatches: `!` forces direct, `?` forces model.

flow.note: Read line from LineEditor
Strip `!`/`?` prefix if present
Try to resolve first word as program; if fails → return NotACommand
Check if line reads as English, not a command (e.g. 'who is alice')
Direct: exec program on terminal; Model: route to engine

features.name: agent-turn-loop
features.description: Model invocation: maintain conversation history, execute tool calls, observe output, iterate until done or user aborts.

flow.note: User types intent (routed to model)
Prepare session + prompt; build request to LLM
Send conversation history + request to Claude API
Parse tool calls from response; dispatch each via tools.rs
Execute tool, capture output (or error)
Append tool result, invoke LLM again; repeat until stop_reason=end_turn
Render final text (markdown → terminal); record to history

features.name: background-coordinator-runs
features.description: Spawn durable background workers for long-running tasks; attach/detach to steer; resume with context preservation.

flow.note: User types work-signal intent or `:dispatch` command
Launch container or subprocess with aish re-exec
Coordinator manages multi-turn loop, journaling, attachment
User attaches to see activity; typed lines are steered via tell-mailbox
When worker finishes, user can type to resume with new context
Worker returns structured output (json or rendered text)

features.name: persistent-memory
features.description: Store and recall facts across sessions; agent reads/writes via remember/recall tools.

flow.note: User or agent calls remember(content, tags); stored in db.memories
Compute embedding via model; store in sqlite-vec
Embed query; search top-K memories by cosine similarity
Recalled memories injected into system prompt for turn

features.name: mcp-skill-integration
features.description: Load MCP servers + SKILL.md packs; advertise tools and skills in model prompts.

flow.note: Connect to servers in ~/.aish/.mcp.json (stdio transport)
Call tools/list; cache definitions for dispatch
Walk ~/.aish/skills/; parse SKILL.md frontmatter
Append tools + skills to system prompt; model can reference
Dispatch MCP tool calls via mcp__server__tool pattern

testing.unit: Inline `#[test]` and `#[tokio::test]` in source files; run with `cargo test --lib`
testing.integration: tests/ directory; routes, dispatch routing, oracle tests (bash compatibility checks)
testing.fixtures: tests/golden/ (golden snapshot files); test data embedded in test functions
testing.run: cargo test --all (unit + integration + doc tests); CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 for low-memory machines

infrastructure.name: github-actions-ci
infrastructure.purpose: Test suite (cargo test), linting (clippy, fmt), security audit (deny.toml), and release builds

infrastructure.name: docker-worker-image
infrastructure.purpose: Ephemeral containers for background coordinator runs; includes Rust toolchain + aish binary

infrastructure.name: makefile-build
infrastructure.purpose: Development targets: build, install, test, lint, clean, register-shell

dependencies.name: tokio
dependencies.why: Async runtime for concurrent tool execution, model invocation, worker management, signal handling

dependencies.name: rustyline
dependencies.why: REPL line editor with completion, history, and hints (fish-style ghost text)

dependencies.name: mistralrs
dependencies.why: Optional: local LLM inference (Qwen3-1.7B GGUF) when --backend local is used; lazy-loaded from HF cache

dependencies.name: sqlite-vec
dependencies.why: Vector similarity search for persistent memory recall; embeddings stored alongside history in aish.db

dependencies.name: rusqlite
dependencies.why: SQLite bindings for history, memories, and worker state persistence

dependencies.name: anyhow
dependencies.why: Error handling throughout; flexible Result<T> with context

goals: Provide a shell that routes real commands (binaries) directly and intent to Claude, eliminating the need to remember syntax
Support persistent background workers that can be attached/detached and resumed with context
Extend seamlessly via MCP servers and SKILL.md packs without code changes
Maintain full transparency: all tool calls, model prompts, and decisions are auditable
Support both cloud (Claude API) and local (mistral.rs GGUF) inference
notes: This is the main aish REPL + coordinator orchestrator. The architecture splits the interactive frontend (repl.rs) from the core execution engine (engine.rs) to enable future evolutions to a full login shell. Background workers (coordinator.rs + container.rs) are spawned as separate aish processes that manage their own multi-turn loops. All state is serialized in SQLite (aish.db) for durability and recall across sessions.
